ne. A UI-authored
suite has no declared id, so no file can claim it. Resolve is never by name.

File `passThreshold` is a fract
ion; the hosted suite grades on a percent. The\nconversion refuses rather than approximates. A file count above **10**\n(`repetiti

ons` in a `schemaVersion: "1"` file, `iterations` in `"2"`) is
refused by name (`REPETITIONS_CAP`) and is not clamped.

**W
hich vocabulary the sync speaks is the deployment's call.** Before writing\nanything, the CLI reads `GET /capabilities` once. A de
ployment that advertises\n`vocabulary.version: 2` gets every request with `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary: 2`\nand case bodies spelled c
anonically — `iterations` (the exact count),\n`legacyIterations` (the legacy floor, the same number) and `assertions` —\ninstead o
f `repetitions` / `iterations` / `checks`. A deployment without the\ncapability block, or without the capabilities route at all, i
s spoken to in\nvocabulary 1, byte-for-byte as before. Nothing in the file changes either way:\nthe dialect of the file and the vo

cabulary of the wire are independent.

Cases are synced in batches of at most 100 (`create_eval_cases`). Every
declared case is
created or updated, including `disabled: true` rows. A case\nthe file **no longer declares** is deleted from the hosted suite bef
ore\nlaunch. A case the file still declares but marks `disabled: true` is **kept,\nwith its history** — it is simply left out of t

he launch, so parking a flaky
test does not destroy its past results and re-enabling it later resumes the
same case.
The run is
scoped to the enabled cases either way. A file with no enabled\ncases is refused (`NO_ENABLED_CASES`) rather than launching the w
hole\npersisted suite. `--case` may only name an enabled case. A later run updates\nexisting cases by declared id and creates new
ones. An enabled case that\noverrides `passThreshold` is refused: hosted grading is suite-wide. A\ndisabled case with the same ove
rride is ignored, matching how repetitions\nare checked. Authored\n`defaults.toolPolicy` and non-empty `defaults.validity` gates a
re refused at\nhosted CLI launch (`TOOL_POLICY_UNSUPPORTED` / the corresponding validity\nrefusal). Hosted platform-authored suite
s do not currently have a backend\ntool-policy field or enforcement path, so the CLI does not upload a suite that\nwould claim tho
se guarantees. When supported by an eval runner, `toolPolicy`\nis enforced at execution time with denied tools kept visible but bl
ocked;\nserver annotations are advisory and **UNTRUSTED**. The file's default count\n(`defaults.repetitions`, or `defaults.iterati
ons` in `schemaVersion: \"2\"`) is\ninherited per case and is not uploaded as a suite `minIterations` floor.\nAuthored `defaults.s
ystemPrompt` and `defaults.temperature` are uploaded as\nexecution defaults; omitted fields stay omitted so the platform applies i
ts\nown defaults. `target.hosts` and `target.environment` are attached before\nlaunch. A file environment takes precedence over fi
le hosts for that launch,\nwhile an explicit CLI target takes precedence over both. When an explicit CLI\ntarget is provided (for
example `--host`), the file's `target.hosts` are\n**not** synchronized to the suite's persisted host attachments — the suite\nkeep
s whatever hosts it already has. Host attachment synchronization only\nruns when no explicit CLI target overrides the file. Enviro

nment attachment
synchronization is unaffected and always runs.

Without `--idempotency-key`, the CLI mints a fresh UUID for ev
ery invocation\nand prints it to stderr before launch (`Eval idempotency key: <key>`). Each\ninvocation therefore starts and bills
a new run. To retry a launch whose\nresponse was lost — without starting a second run — pass the key that was\nprinted: `--idempo

tency-key <printed-key>`. A replay is marked `deduped` in
the receipt and human output. `--notes` is not part of the key.

####
# Imported cases: live tool resolution, and per-run approval\n\nEvery file run performs the same live check `eval validate --proje
ct` performs,\n**before it writes anything**. It is not opt-in and there is no flag to skip\nit. A file with no deterministic `too

lCall` steps asks no question and pays no
round trip.

What happens when a deterministic reference does not resolve depends on

the
case:

| Case | Outcome |
| - | - |
| Selected (enabled, and named by `--case` if you used it) | The launch **refuses bef
ore the suite is synced** — nothing is written and nothing is billed |\n| Imported, not selected | Its claim is rewritten to `unre
solved` (keeping `sourceCaseKey`) and it is **still persisted**, so the hosted record says what MCPJam found rather than still ass
erting a claim about a missing tool |\n| Native, not selected | Left exactly as authored. A hand-written case never acquires an `i
mport` block from this — \"somebody wrote this\" and \"something converted this\" are different facts |\n\nEach target is checked
on **its own** server set. `--host` is checked against\nthat host's configured servers rather than the file's, because that is the
set\nthe run connects — validating `target.servers` would approve a tool the host\ncannot reach. A host the FILE declares uses it
s own `servers` list when it\ndeclares one (those are attached to the host before launch) and the host's\nconfigured set when the
field is omitted. An explicitly empty `servers: []`\nis a real, empty set — it clears the attachment before launch — and is\nvalid
ated as such, never as an omitted field. A step that pins `serverId` is resolved by id;\n`serverName` is a display fallback and ne

ver overrides it.

If the run's target set cannot be enumerated before the suite exists
(`--all-targets`, `--compose-*`), or a
host does not report a server set, or a\nhost pins a server the project no longer has, the launch refuses rather than\nassuming th

e references are fine.

`--case` accepts a hosted row id, which does not exist yet when this check
runs. A selector this stage
cannot map is therefore treated as possibly naming\nany enabled case, so an unresolved reference still refuses; the launcher\n> ##

# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects —

diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It
works today and we use it ourselves, but\n> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change — including in\n> brea
king ways — while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> rea
der](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or

> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys

)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right b

ack on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hoste

d/overview.md) projects — from CI, scripts, or your own agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* *
*Discover your resources** — list your projects, their servers, eval\n suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes ne

ed is
 self-serve
* **Validate a server** — connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot
* **Run the doctor** — the
probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\n* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **
List tools, prompts, and resources** — the server's MCP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and g
et the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource** by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one
JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients** — list, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cu
rsor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connect
